acip: GNYIS PA 'GYUR PHYAG NI, MDO SNGAGS KYI CHOS BSTAN PA'I (BKA' DRIN) DANG (MNYAM) PA GZHAN (MED) PA'I (BLA MA) STE GONG MA'AM LHAG MA (DAM PA) STE MCHOG (RNAMS KYI ZHABS LA PHYAG 'TSAL ZHING SKYABS SU MCHI'O,),
wylie: gnyis pa 'gyur phyag ni, mdo sngags kyi chos bstan pa'i (bka' drin) dang (mnyam) pa gzhan (med) pa'i (bla ma) ste gong ma'am lhag ma (dam pa) ste mchog (rnams kyi zhabs la phyag 'tshal zhing skyabs su mchi'o,)
english: This brings us to our second point--the translator's obeisance.  The text begins now with I bow to the blessed feet of my "holy"--which here means "supreme"--Lamas, who are matchless in Their kindness.  This kindness consists of the fact that they have granted to us the Dharma of both the open and secret teachings.  Remember that the word lama itself means higher, or beyond.  And I come to my Lamas for shelter.
